label: Exercise 11.3 — Validating an approximate MPC with Hoeffding
source_text:
Exercise 11.3 — Validating an approximate MPC with Hoeffding
      
      
        Take $\delta_h=0.01$, $\mu_{\mathrm{crit}}=0.99$ as in Hertneck et al. (a) Your network violates the error bound on about $0.2\%$ of trajectories ($\tilde\mu\approx0.998$). How many validation trajectories are needed with the two-sided bound, and with the one-sided one? (b) With the paper's $p=34\,980$, how many failures can the test tolerate? (c) You may retrain and re-validate up to $K=5$ times, using fresh independent IID validation trajectories for each trained controller: which per-attempt confidence keeps the overall one at $0.99$, and what happens to $p$ in (a)? (d) State precisely what a passed test guarantees.
        
          Show answer
          
            (a) Need $\epsilon_h\le0.998-0.99=0.008$. Two-sided: $p\ge\ln200/(2\cdot0.008^2)=\ln200/(1.28\cdot10^{-4})\approx41\,393.1$, so $41\,394$. One-sided: $\ln100/(1.28\cdot10^{-4})\approx35\,977.9$, so $35\,978$.
            (b) $\epsilon_h=\sqrt{\ln200/(2\cdot34\,980)}\approx0.0087025$, so the exact test requires $\tilde\mu\ge0.99+\epsilon_h\approx0.9987025$, i.e. at least $34\,935$ successes: at most 45 failures. (The reported $0.9987$ is rounded; exactly $0.9987$ would fail by about $3\cdot10^{-6}$.)
            (c) Union bound: $0.01/5=0.002$ per attempt, so $p\ge\ln(1000)/(1.28\cdot10^{-4})\approx53\,966.8$, i.e. $53\,967$ (two-sided): about 30% more samples buy honesty about repeated testing.
            (d) With probability at least $1-\delta_h$ over the validation data, with probability at least $\mu_{\mathrm{crit}}$, a fresh initial condition from the same $\Omega$ gives a trajectory that enters $X_f$ in finite time and satisfies $\|\pi_{\mathrm{approx}}-\pi_{\mathrm{MPC}}\|_\infty\le\eta$ at every step before entry; on it Theorem 5 gives constraint satisfaction up to that entry, after which the terminal controller $k_f$ keeps the state in $X_f$ and gives convergence (Remark 6). The guarantee is for this switched controller: $\pi_{\mathrm{approx}}$ itself is not validated inside $X_f$. Nothing is said for other initial distributions.

claims.statement_in_prose: The theorem obtains true one-sided confidence from the genuine generic Bernoulli Hoeffding theorem, evaluates the actual exponent exactly to delta, then proves set containment into the false-acceptance implication event. The final probability statement is derived, not assumed. It is frequentist over validation data for each fixed true law, not a posterior or a conditional-on-acceptance probability. The true two-sided bounded independent average theorem is instantiated with actual Bernoulli support and mean derived from HasLaw. Actual measurable complement probabilities yield a true good-data event, and actual absolute-error algebra gives the acceptance implication. The literal factor2/1 and per-attempt factor1000 radii are explicitly linked to the source. Genuine log enclosures certify the three displayed approximations and derive the exact natural minima41394,35978,53967. The corrected actual denominators are explicitly grouped. All numerical equalities remaining in this clause are exact rational identities. The actual radius is strictly between.00870250 and.00870251, which certifies the source approximation. The actual acceptance threshold is retained symbolically as.99+radius. A true iff proves exactly at most45 failures and34935 successes; the actual positive gap above.9987 lies between2e-6 and3e-6, consistent with the source warning. No rounded threshold is substituted for the true test. These actual exact rational identities/inequalities and sample-count minima are proved. They do not by themselves derive a measure-theoretic overall error bound for adaptively retrained controllers or justify reuse of validation data. A genuine product/Fubini argument integrates actual section bad-event probabilities over arbitrary histories. Those section probabilities are derived from the fixed-model Hoeffding confidence theorem and measurable complements, not given as final confidence. Actual HasLaw maps each history/fresh-data pair into this product, and a true finite union bound for the5 events plus complement gives simultaneous confidence>=.99. Every acceptance implication holds on that same good event, so any chosen attempt there inherits it. This is not a posterior or conditional-on-stopping confidence interpretation. The corrected question now explicitly requires fresh independent IID validation trajectories for each trained controller, matching the genuine conditional-history/product-law assumptions. The true recurrent trajectory is defined and its measurability proved by induction. The actual successful-initial-state set is a countable union over finite entry times of countable measurable pre-entry/error conditions. Its complement indicator has a Bernoulli failure law derived from its actual mu probability. Composition with the actual IID initial draws derives independence and HasLaw for the failure outcomes, then the true two-sided Hoeffding acceptance guarantee yields mu(good)>=critical on a data event of probability>=1-delta. Applying that generic event wrapper to the separately proved measurable goodInitialStates models the literal before-entry protocol. No MPC invariance or convergence is inferred from this statistical event alone.
